subject: Time-consuming matrix operations vs reduction of parameter space

messages.author: 3d2186e6d007f6a7
messages.subject: Time-consuming matrix operations vs reduction of parameter space
parts:
Hello all,

I am facing a problem where I tried to reduce the number of parameters in optimization but also increasing the number of operations in each optimization step. Below is a toy example:
  • Data likelihood layer: Y_ij ~ Bernoulli(X_ij, theta), i = 1, ..., n and j = 1, ..., q, where i is the i-th time step, and j is one of the dimensions of X
  • Random effects: X ~ Multivariate Wiener Process(theta), where X is q-dimensional
  • Prior: theta ~ p(theta) which contains the multivariate Wiener process covariance 
So X is random, and theta is the fixed effects. 

When I have a long time window and X is high dimension, then both n and q are large numbers so there are (nxq) elements of X to integrate out in each step of inner optimization. 

My idea: using the basis expansion for multivariate wiener process and write X as X = phi *Xi, where the random effects X is n x q, basis function design matrix phi is n x m, and the coefficient matrix Xi is m x q. A known result is that the rows of Xi are iid q-dimensional MVN, so now I have effectively make Xi the random effects in place of X.

Using this basis expansion I have reduced the dimension of random effects from n x q to m x q, where m should be much smaller than n, e.g., 50 times less, so this achieves a reduction in parameter space. However, to reconstruct X I have an additional matrix operation in each step of the inner optimization: X = phi *Xi.

I was hoping that the reduction in computational time due to a smaller parameter space can compensate for the additional computational time due to the matrix operation, but this turns out not the case - the matrix operation takes up so much time.

This is what I wrote in the cpp template for matrix operation and I timed it using std::chrono::high_resolution_clock:
   
   DATA_ARRAY(Phi);
   PARAMETER_ARRAY(xi);
   matrix<Type> Phi_xi = Phi.transpose().matrix() * xi.matrix();

Then this was referenced in the data likelihood calculation as:
  for(int u=0;u<n_trial;u++){
    for(int j=0;j<n_bin;j++){
      Type nu_x = nu * (Phi_xi(j, u) * sqrt(T) + alpha*dt*(j+1) - Nt*k)

whereas in the template without basis expansion I simply replaced Phi_xi(j, u) by X(j, u):

  PARAMETER_ARRAY(X);
  for(int u=0;u<n_trial;u++){
    for(int j=0;j<n_bin;j++){
      Type nu_x = nu * (X(j, u) * sqrt(T) + alpha*dt*(j+1) - Nt*k)

Thank you so much in advance! I am very sorry for this long post. Would really appreciate any insight on this! 

Meixi
